cases.name: Square starting grid
cases.description: Four ordered sides expose corners and side midpoints. Explicit seam declarations join repeated cells; matching coordinates alone do not join them.

cases.name: Stretch into rectangles
cases.description: Every actual start, chord and pitch follows R→RR, U→U. The rectangular unit retains the square source and the native substitution receipts.
cases.atlas: Rectangular grid; precursor to B01 and B02

cases.name: Insert a middle course
cases.description: A translated copy of the actual bottom side inserts a course at the existing side midpoints. Existing four sides and their roles are carried unchanged.

cases.name: Shift alternate brick joints
cases.description: The side focus is replaced by a lower joint and a shifted upper joint. Horizontal courses remain actual carried paths. This changes adjacency; it is separate from the preceding stretch.

cases.name: Shear the running bond
cases.description: R→R and U→RU act on the existing brick paths and both period words. The alternating joint topology survives the oblique disposition.

cases.name: Shear the square grid
cases.description: The same complete substitution shears the original square branch. No display-basis change supplies the native slant.

cases.name: Add a third tie family
cases.description: A new tie joins opposite advertised corners through the actual two-side displacement. The third direction creates triangular circuits. Merely shearing a four-sided grid did not create those ties.

cases.name: Add crossing diagonal ties
cases.description: Two diagonal paths are composed from actual horizontal and vertical half-side words. Their centre is an explicit endpoint on both paths, so the local seam contract can join it.

cases.name: Stretch the diagonal network
cases.description: The previous diagonal network and its pitches follow the actual stretch. Its tied centre and diagonal histories remain; a second finished atlas endpoint is never substituted.

cases.name: Pair narrow orthogonal strips
cases.description: The bottom and reversed left side are subdivided one/three and each reused with a one-reach offset. All narrow-strip crossings have actual path endpoint roles.

cases.name: Turn paired strips into oblique ribbons
cases.description: R→RRU and U→LLU carry the paired-strip incidence and both periods into an oblique ribbon arrangement. The narrow and wide intervals remain native repeated participation.

cases.name: Expose corner inset sites
cases.description: Each two-reach chord is refined into its two actual move occurrences. The square outline is unchanged while the sites needed for a corner cut become explicit.

cases.name: Chamfer the square corners
cases.description: Corner participation is replaced by diagonal bridge chords between the inset sites. Middle side chords remain actual source words. This is a chord/topology edit, with an explicit closed contour, rather than an affine deformation of four corners.
cases.atlas: B06-like octagon and interstitial diamond field

cases.name: Expose basket contact intervals
cases.description: Only the long rectangle chords are subdivided. The outline remains rectangular, while future side contacts become actual path vertices. The next assembly publishes their new endpoint roles.

cases.name: Assemble alternating basket rectangles
cases.description: The actual rectangle is reused twice directly and twice through its quarter substitution, with four retained translation receipts. Split side contacts leave square gaps. This assembly branch has different path topology from running brick.
cases.atlas: B02-like basket rectangles and square gaps

cases.name: Shear the basket assembly
cases.description: The complete basket assembly is sheared with all contacts and periods. Its four-copy construction stays distinct from the sheared running-bond branch even where a coarse directional read agrees.

cases.name: Try a wider shear
cases.description: A sibling generated from the same square substitutes U→RRU. The explicit binding and the native word receipts retain this larger offset separately from the first shear.
cases.atlas: New sibling of the oblique-grid family

cases.name: Try an opposed brick shear
cases.description: The same running-bond parent receives U→LU. Its alternating joints remain, while the shear route differs from the earlier R→R, U→RU branch.
cases.atlas: New sibling of the oblique-brick family

cases.name: Try a tighter ribbon disposition
cases.description: The paired-strip parent receives R→RU, U→LU. The one/three intervals and explicit crossing ports are reused with a different complete native substitution.
cases.atlas: New sibling of the ribbon family

limits: Historical basis is an actual retained participant, not proof that the current graph still has every ancestral property.
Transforms, endpoint-preserving refinements, topology edits and assembly are different witnessed transitions.
History-blind candidates use actual shared incidence and qualitative headings; they do not receive recipe labels or construction history.
Incidence support is a non-draining coarse question with explicit many-to-one stroke correspondence; drawing histories remain available.
Boundary obligations and unsearched candidates remain distinct from failed interior seams.
Atlas references name construction families; exact identity with every source engraving is not claimed.
No regular polygon metric, universal pattern recognition, aesthetic score or autonomous learning is established.
